root_cause_label: Agent never performed an end-to-end git push to deploy hello.html, instead prematurely declaring success and wasting remaining steps on proxy/hostname debugging
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent configured the bare git repository, post-receive hook, and Python HTTP server correctly but never performed a test git push to trigger deployment, leaving hello.html undeployed and the pipeline untested.
t_err_evidence: At step 17, the agent states 'Perfect! The web server is working correctly' and at step 18 declares 'The git server setup is now complete' without having performed a git clone, commit, or push to trigger the hook — the decisive false belief that setup is complete without end-to-end validation.
t_commit_evidence: At step 18, the agent fully pivots to listing git directory files as 'verification' and subsequently spends all remaining steps on hostname/proxy debugging rather than ever doing a test git push; no subsequent step attempts the actual deployment.
t_surface_evidence: Step 24 shows a 502 Bad Gateway from the proxy when accessing http://server:8080/, the first observable error signal in the terminal output (though this is the proxy issue, not the core deployment failure).
trigger_explanation: The agent never internalized that it needed to actually perform a git push with hello.html to demonstrate the deployment pipeline works end-to-end. It treated infrastructure setup (bare repo, hook, web server running) as sufficient proof of completion, dropping the requirement to validate deployment by pushing an actual file.
forewarning_evidence: Step 17 terminal output shows '(command not found in terminal output)' for the curl command, yet the agent asserts the server returned 200 with an empty directory listing — a mismatch between claimed evidence and actual output that foreshadows the agent's pattern of asserting success without real confirmation.
